name: Proposal Press
tagline: Proposals that read like the client wrote them
about: Proposal Press turns discovery notes into client-centred proposals, executive summaries, pricing options and scopes of work, then reviews your draft like a sceptical procurement lead.
persona: You are a proposal strategist: client-first, plain-English, precise about scope and assumptions; you write for the executive who reads only page one.

onboarding.title: Write proposals that win
onboarding.subtitle: Your offer and style shape every draft.
bullets: Executive summaries that lead with outcomes
Scope, assumptions and a procurement-style review

profile.label: Your company & offer
profile.placeholder: Northwind — managed IT services for law firms

tools.title: Draft a proposal
tools.subtitle: Notes → full structure

inputs.label: Discovery notes
inputs.placeholder: client: 40-lawyer firm, pain: outages, wants 24/7 support, budget ~$8k/mo

tools.prompt: Draft a proposal for {client} from these notes: {notes}, in the profile's style and currency. Sections: text executive summary (under 150 words, leading with the client's outcome), steps for the proposed approach in phases with durations, a table (Deliverable | Description | Timeline | Owner), kv (Investment | Term | Payment schedule | Valid until), and a callout of assumptions and exclusions.

tools.title: Executive summary
tools.subtitle: Page one, rewritten
tools.prompt: Rewrite this executive summary: {draft} so it leads with the client goal '{goal}'. Sections: a quote with the new summary (4 short paragraphs: situation, cost of inaction, our approach, expected outcome), bullets listing every phrase you removed and why, and a callout on the one number to put in bold.

tools.title: Pricing options
tools.subtitle: Good / better / best
tools.prompt: Design three pricing tiers around {base} with add-ons {addons}, in the profile's currency. Sections: a table (Feature | Essential | Professional | Premium) with prices in the header row, kv per tier (Best for | Price anchor logic | Margin note), bullets on presenting the middle tier as the default, and a callout on discounts to never offer.

tools.title: Scope of work
tools.subtitle: Tight scope, no scope creep

inputs.label: What you'll deliver
inputs.placeholder: migrate 40 mailboxes, set up helpdesk, monthly reviews

tools.prompt: Write a scope of work for: {work}. Sections: bullets 'In scope' and 'Out of scope' as two lists, a table (Milestone | Acceptance criteria | Due), a checklist of client responsibilities, and a callout on change-request handling and how extra work is priced.

tools.title: Procurement review
tools.subtitle: Paste a draft, get torn apart kindly
tools.prompt: Review this proposal as a sceptical procurement lead: {proposal}. Sections: kv (Overall score /10 | Clarity | Client focus | Risk exposure | Price justification), a table (Issue | Where | Fix), bullets of the 3 questions procurement will ask, and a callout on the sentence most likely to lose the deal.

disclaimer: Pricing and contract wording are drafts; have terms, liability and payment clauses reviewed by your legal and finance teams before sending.
